Recently, Jindie Shikong and the Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences jointly achieved a significant technological breakthrough—the RISC-V AI CPU chip K3 successfully runs the OpenHarmony 6.1 system, making it the world's first RISC-V architecture chip to support OpenHarmony 6.1. This marks the adaptation of RISC-V chips and the open-source HarmonyOS entering a new phase of full autonomy and dual open-source in both "chip + system."  

During this adaptation process, both parties leveraged their respective technical strengths and collaborated deeply:  
▲ The Institute of Software provided OpenHarmony system-level technical support, completing RISC-V architecture compatibility and core component porting.  
▲ Jindie Shikong handled the underlying hardware adaptation, driver development, and performance optimization for the K3 chip.  

This combination truly achieves full-stack autonomy from chip to system, providing a more secure and controllable solution for smart terminals, IoT, and other fields.  

OpenHarmony 6.1 is the Long-Term Support (LTS) version released by the OpenHarmony community. Compared to previous versions, its advantages include:  
▲ Up to 3 years of official maintenance support, ensuring long-term stable iteration and making it more suitable for deployment in enterprise production environments.  
▲ Significantly enhanced application development capabilities, supporting more refined application control and smoother dynamic effects.  
▲ Upgraded system-level functionality and multimedia experience, improving system perception.

Esto marca que la adaptación entre los chips RISC-V y el sistema operativo de código abierto Harmony ha entrado oficialmente en una nueva etapa de "chip + sistema", completamente autónoma y de doble código abierto. Durante este proceso de adaptación, ambas partes aprovecharon sus respectivas ventajas técnicas y colaboraron en profundidad: el Instituto de Software proporcionó OpenHarmony.

excerpt_i18n.en:
A "No Pretense, No Formality" Private Gathering  
On the afternoon of April 11, 15 people gathered behind closed doors at the Z·Pilot space in Nantou Ancient City, Shenzhen, for a four-hour conversation. There was no live streaming, no recording, no PowerPoint presentations, and no company introductions. The first words upon entering were "Who am I," followed immediately by speaking the truth.  

This was the first Conclave organized by HardTech Community—a closed-door meeting specifically designed for entrepreneurs in the sports technology sector. Attendees included creators of smart tennis robots, action cameras, skiing equipment, rehabilitation medical devices, and several investors.  

Not a single word typically spoken at public product launches was uttered here.  

Who is HardTech Community?  
HardTech Community is an investor community under Leiphone, focusing on hard tech sectors such as AI hardware, robotics, and smart mobility. We don’t host large conferences or pitch events—we do one thing: bring together those truly immersed in these fields into a room for an afternoon of candid conversation.  

HardTech Conclave is a closed-door meeting series co-organized by Leiphone’s HardTech Community and investment institutions. Each session is strictly limited to 15 participants, inviting only those with genuine entrepreneurial experience or deep industry insights. No company introductions, no business card exchanges—just discussions on insights and challenges.  

The co-organizer of this session, Different Capital, originates from the family office of one of Alibaba’s founders and focuses on cross-border e-commerce, AI software and hardware, and robotics. They have invested in companies like Walker Extraordinary, Inhands Power, DeepGaze Technology, and Squirrel Power, and possess a systematic framework for evaluating the sports hardware sector.  

Three questions were discussed over four hours.

Sin transmisión en vivo, sin grabaciones, sin presentaciones en PowerPoint, sin introducciones corporativas. La primera frase al entrar fue «quién soy», y la segunda comenzó a decir la verdad. excerpt_i18n.en:
Author | Wu You  Editor | Yu Kuai  
Imagine a specific scenario: you wake up at 9 a.m., open your phone, and find 47 notifications piled up from over a dozen apps. Checking and handling them one by one is time-consuming and makes it easy to miss the key points.  

At this moment, a hardware product called YoooClaw comes into play. It integrates information across applications, automatically organizing it into a tiered board categorized as urgent, to be handled, or for awareness only, making information clear at a glance. It also incorporates AI capabilities to deeply analyze the impact of information, directly providing users with actionable suggestions. YoooClaw helps users transform chaotic notification streams into clear decision-making flows, allowing them to see at first glance what needs to be handled most urgently each day, becoming their most capable action partner.  

Unlike other products such as Plaud, YoooClaw does not acquire user context through chat interfaces or build user memory through recordings. Instead, it extracts scattered, noisy information from users’ daily behaviors—such as notifications, cross-application actions, fragmented tasks, and lightweight records—refining it into personal context and organizing it into more valuable inputs. This makes AI more useful in real-world scenarios.  

Xiao Ruizhe, the founder of YoooClaw, co-founded the open-source website-building software PHPWind while studying at Beijing Jiaotong University, which was later acquired by Alibaba. After joining Alibaba, he participated in the entire lifecycle of Aliyun OS, from its establishment to its integration into Banma. He later joined Huawei’s Smart Selection Car team, deeply engaging in product definition, pricing, target audience analysis, and gross margin calculations.

Revisarlas y gestionarlas una por una consume tiempo y dificulta identificar lo prioritario. En este momento, un producto de hardware llamado YoooClaw integra toda la información de diferentes aplicaciones, organizándola automáticamente en un tablero clasificado por urgencia, tareas pendientes y solo para conocimiento, haciendo que la información sea clara de un vistazo.
